newsitem.title: ITALY: IMF's Camdessus urges Italy towards more reforms.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Camdessus urges Italy towards more reforms.

text.p: Italy must have more courage to undertake social and economic reforms if it wants to be among the first wave of nation's into European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), International Monetary Fund (IMF) chief Michel Camdessus said.
In an interview in the financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore on Saturday, Camdessus said he saw difficulties for Italy as it faced EMU and the increasing globalisation of financial markets.

"Italian economic figures show an unemployment rate of 12 percent and prospects for growth of just above one percent in 1997. I do not see how this situation could be characterised as optimistic," he said in the interview that took place in Washington.

He added that Italy needed to reduce its public debt, reform pensions, and make unions more responsible in wage rounds. He urged further privatisations and other measures to put Italy on track to join the first round of EMU nations.

On Italy's chances of joining the first wave of EMU, he said this was still possible. Much depends on the will of the Italian government and the people, and there are still many dangers ahead and much depends on the 1998 Italian budget, he said.

He said Italy had managed to get inflation down and must continue to show it can keep inflation low. The last official consumer price index figures showed the inflation rate at 2.6 percent in December and preliminary CPI figures for January showed an unchanged 2.6 percent rate.
He declined direct comment on Italy's often-criticised banking system, but stressed that the restructuring of banking systems was a priority for all in the world.
